meta.purpose: VNG Interconnect: P3200 (Transco segment) duplicates P5990; merge ruled by Baird 2026-11-07. P5990 values moved to the 2021 Interconnect scope. The earlier Header Improvement Project is split out as its own cancelled row (discovery-header-improvement-20261107); P5990's route goes with it and P5990 gets a trimmed route candidate (route-creation-vng-hip-20261107).

resolutions.recommendation: Merge P3200 into P5990 (Baird ruled 2026-11-07). Follow the Update SOP merge steps: copy P3200's refs onto P5990, move P3200 and its operators/owners row to the Removed tabs, then delete both rows. Regenerate the Transcontinental Gas Pipeline and VNG Interconnect wiki pages afterwards. The earlier Header Improvement Project is staged as its own cancelled row (discovery-header-improvement-20261107), so it is not merged into either row.

verifications.note: EIA's natural gas pipeline projects table, August 2026 release. The Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 1143, lists VNG Interconnect by Virginia Natural Gas: cancelled, 10 miles, cost 205 (the column is in millions of dollars), 245 million cubic feet per day of added capacity. The note says it is an expansion to an interconnect with Transco.

Prince William Times article from December 17, 2020. It says the Virginia Natural Gas Interconnect is a $205 million project with about six miles of pipeline in Prince William County and four miles in Fauquier County, nearly 10 miles in all. It calls it a scaled back version of the Header Improvement Project, which the State Corporation Commission had dismissed weeks earlier.

resolutions.researcher_notes: This row is the VNG Interconnect, filed as a segment of Transco. P5990 is the same project under the same name, with its own wiki page. Both are Virginia Natural Gas projects in Prince William and Fauquier counties, cancelled in 2021. Virginia Natural Gas would have connected to Transco, but Transco did not own it. The values that differ between the two rows are staged on P5990.

verifications.note: Virginia Natural Gas's public application to the State Corporation Commission for the VNG Interconnect, December 2020, read as a May 2024 Wayback copy because the original link now returns 404. It lists the Transco Interconnect Pipeline, about 6.2 miles of 30 inch steel pipe, and the Quantico Parallel Pipe, about 3.5 miles of 30 inch steel pipe.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The 30 inch diameter is right for the VNG Interconnect too. The current ref describes the earlier Header Improvement Project. Virginia Natural Gas's own application for the Interconnect gives 30 inch pipe for both new lines, so it is added as a ref. The value stays.

verifications.note: Virginia Natural Gas press release from December 2020 announcing its application for the VNG Interconnect. It gives about 9.5 miles of pipeline in Prince William and Fauquier counties and a proposed in-service date of December 2023. It also says the Commission dismissed the earlier Header Improvement Project application on December 1.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The planned start was blank. Virginia Natural Gas planned to start service in December 2023, according to its December 2020 press release. The duplicate row P3200 also has 2023, so the year carries over in the merge.
